name: Protein S Acquired Deficiency

criteria.description: Reduced free and total Protein S antigen levels and decreased Protein S activity in plasma
No pathogenic mutations detected in the PROS1 gene indicating acquired rather than inherited deficiency
Presence of underlying conditions known to cause acquired Protein S deficiency such as liver disease, vitamin K deficiency, or autoimmune disorders
History of venous thromboembolism or arterial thrombosis consistent with hypercoagulable state

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Low Protein S activity with absence of PROS1 gene mutations plus clinical evidence of thrombosis or presence of an underlying condition causing acquired deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Testing should be repeated after resolution of acute illness or anticoagulation therapy to confirm diagnosis.

searchTerms: frequent deep vein or lung clots
multiple episodes of vein blood clots

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deep vein thrombosis of lower extremities

common.symptomName: Skin necrosis at anticoagulant injection sites
searchTerms: skin death at blood thinner injection sites

occasional.symptomName: Headache related to cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
searchTerms: pain due to cerebral venous thrombosis
head pain linked to brain blood clots
bleeding in adrenal glands from clots

laboratory: Decreased free and total Protein S antigen levels
Reduced Protein S functional activity assays
Normal PROS1 gene sequencing (no inherited mutation)
imaging: Ultrasound Doppler showing deep vein thrombosis
CT pulmonary angiography demonstrating pulmonary embolism
MRI/MRV for cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
genetic: Absence of pathogenic mutations in PROS1 gene
other: Identification of underlying conditions such as liver disease, vitamin K deficiency, or autoimmune disorders contributing to acquired deficiency

distinguishingFeatures: No reduction in Protein S levels

redFlags: Thrombosis in unusual sites (cerebral, renal, adrenal veins)
Skin necrosis after initiation of anticoagulation
references: Orphanet: Protein S Acquired Deficiency - ORPHA:26349
